# Multitude — full text dump

> Free, open-source Unity editor extension: several prefabs open at once, each in its own window.
> Repo: https://github.com/gabriel96x1/Multitude   Landing: https://gabriel96x1.github.io/Multitude/   License: LGPL-3.0 or AGPL-3.0   Version: 0.1.0


# === README (README.md) ===

# Multitude

Edit several prefab assets at the same time, each one in its own window, without touching the scene you
have open and without going through Unity's prefab stage.

Each window owns an isolated session: its own hierarchy, its own preview, its own inspector. Changes
stay inside the window until you press **Apply**; **Revert** throws them away. If the prefab file
changed on disk in the meantime, Apply refuses to overwrite it and asks you what to do.

![A Multitude window playing a VFX prefab](docs/assets/img/vfx-window.png)

**Landing page:** open `docs/index.html` locally, or enable GitHub Pages with *Settings → Pages →
Deploy from branch → `master` / `/docs`* and it will be served at
`https://gabriel96x1.github.io/Multitude/`.

## Requirements

| | |
|---|---|
| Unity | **6000.6** (Unity 6.6) or newer |
| Render pipeline | tested with URP 17.6; nothing pipeline specific in the code |
| Platform | Editor only, no runtime assembly |

## Install

**Git URL (recommended):** `Window > Package Manager > + > Add package from git URL...`

```
https://github.com/gabriel96x1/Multitude.git
```

You can pin a version with `#v0.1.0` or a commit hash.

**Released files:** each [release](https://github.com/gabriel96x1/Multitude/releases) carries two files:

| File | How |
|---|---|
| `Multitude-<version>.unitypackage` | drag it into the Unity **Project** window, or double click it. Lands in `Assets/Multitude/` |
| `com.gabs.multitude-<version>.tgz` | `+ > Add package from tarball...` |

Pick **one** route: the `.unitypackage` puts the sources inside your project (easy to tweak, no package
manager, no automatic updates), the package routes install it under `Packages/`. Installing both
compiles the same types twice.

**Local path (development):** in `Packages/manifest.json` of your project add

```json
"com.gabs.multitude": "file:../Multitude"
```

or use `Window > Package Manager > + > Add package from disk...` and pick this folder's `package.json`.

**Build the files yourself:** `./scripts/build-package.sh` runs the tests and writes both artifacts to
`build/`. Details, flags and what each one ships: [Documentation~/BUILDING.md](Documentation~/BUILDING.md).

## Usage

- `Assets > Multitude > Open Prefab in Multitude` (right click a prefab) or
  `Tools > Multitude > Open Selected Prefabs`.
- Preview: left drag orbits, right drag or `Alt`+left pans, the wheel zooms, `F` frames. Double click
  an object in the hierarchy to frame it.
- Drag the separators to resize the hierarchy column and the inspector; double click a separator to
  reset its size. Each window remembers its own layout.
- Particle systems and VFX play in the preview: `Play`/`Pause`, `Restart`, `Loop` and a speed slider.
- `Apply` writes the prefab asset, `Revert` reloads it from disk, closing a dirty window asks first.

Full details, limits and troubleshooting: [Documentation~/MVP.md](Documentation~/MVP.md).

## How it stays isolated

Unity renders any object that lives in a loaded scene, even with `HideAndDontSave`, so preview objects
are created hidden, put on a private layer and taken out of every camera with
`Renderer.forceRenderingOff`. They are switched on only while the preview renders its own frame, and
left over copies are destroyed when scripts reload. Your scene, scene view, game view and prefab stage
never see anything from Multitude.

## Tests

The package ships EditMode tests, included in the `.tgz` and in git URL installs (not in the
`.unitypackage`). To run them, add the package to the testables of your project's
`Packages/manifest.json`:

```json
"testables": ["com.gabs.multitude"]
```

Then open `Window > General > Test Runner > EditMode`.

## Layout

```
package.json                  package manifest (Unity 6000.6+)
Editor/Core/                  asset validation, snapshots, edit session
Editor/UI/                    preview view, preview host, VFX playback, hierarchy, inspector
Editor/Windows/               the per prefab window
Editor/Commands/              menu entries
Tests/Editor/                 EditMode tests
Documentation~/MVP.md         usage, limits and troubleshooting
docs/                         landing page (English in /, Spanish in /es/, GitHub Pages ready)
scripts/                      local packaging: build-package.sh + PackageExporter.cs
```

## License

Dual licensed: **LGPL-3.0** or **AGPL-3.0**, your choice per copy or distribution — the notice is in
[LICENSE](LICENSE) and the full texts in [`licenses/`](licenses).

- **LGPL-3.0** (`licenses/LGPL-3.0.txt`, which builds on `licenses/GPL-3.0.txt`) lets you ship
  Multitude inside a closed product, as long as the library itself — and any modification you make to
  it — stays under the LGPL and the user can replace it. This is the option that fits a sold or closed
  Unity tool.
- **AGPL-3.0** (`licenses/AGPL-3.0.txt`) is strong copyleft and also covers offering the tool as a
  service.

Neither option is permissive in the MIT sense: modifications to the library stay open. Weigh that
before bundling it into a commercial asset.


# === BUILDING (Documentation~/BUILDING.md) ===

# Building the package

Everything happens locally. There is no CI: `scripts/build-package.sh` runs the test suite and produces
the two installable files, and the release is uploaded to GitHub by hand.

```bash
./scripts/build-package.sh
```

| Output | Install it with |
|---|---|
| `build/Multitude-<version>.unitypackage` | drag it into the Unity **Project** window (or double click it with the project open). Lands in `Assets/Multitude/` |
| `build/com.gabs.multitude-<version>.tgz` | `Window > Package Manager > + > Add package from tarball...` |

Do not install both at once: the same types would be compiled twice.

## Options

| Flag | Effect |
|---|---|
| `--skip-tests` | export only (the archive is still verified). Warm run: ~5 s |
| `--no-tgz` | skip `npm pack`, `.unitypackage` only |
| `--clean` | wipe `.build/` and reimport from scratch (needed after switching editor patch) |

`UNITY_PATH=/path/to/Unity` overrides the editor. Otherwise the newest
`/Applications/Unity/Hub/Editor/<unity field from package.json>*/Unity.app` is used.

## What the script does

1. Reads `version` and `unity` from `package.json` and picks a matching editor. The editor version is
   part of the throwaway project path, because a `Library/` built by another patch produces import
   errors that look like test failures.
2. Creates (or reuses) `.build/project-<editor version>/`.
3. Copies the package into `Assets/Multitude/`: `Editor/`, `package.json`, `README.md`,
   `CHANGELOG.md`, `LICENSE`, `licenses/` **and** `Tests/`, plus `scripts/PackageExporter.cs` as
   `Assets/CiTools/Editor/`. Root `.meta` files travel too so the GUIDs stay stable.
4. Injects `com.unity.test-framework` into the project manifest. `-createProject` does not ship it in
   Unity 6, and without it the `UNITY_INCLUDE_TESTS` test assembly never compiles — the suite would
   report "0 tests" and look green.
5. Runs the EditMode suite and fails if fewer than 32 tests ran or Unity exits with 2 (failed) or 3
   (never started).
6. Deletes `Tests/` **and** `Tests.meta` (Unity recreates an empty `Tests/` from an orphan `.meta`),
   then exports `Assets/Multitude` with `AssetDatabase.ExportPackage`.
7. Verifies the archive: it must contain the editor asmdef and `package.json`, and must not contain
   `Tests/`, `Documentation~/` or `CiTools/`.
8. Builds the UPM tarball with `git archive HEAD` + `npm pack`, minus `.github/`, `scripts/` and
   `docs/`. The tarball therefore reflects the **last commit**, not the working tree: the script warns
   when tracked files are dirty, and so does the `.unitypackage` if you commit after building.

Logs live in `.build/` (`create.log`, `tests.log`, `export.log`, `results.xml`). Both `.build/` and
`build/` are gitignored.

## What ships, and what cannot

The `.unitypackage` contains `Editor/`, `package.json`, `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `LICENSE` and
`licenses/`.

- `Tests/` is **not** in the `.unitypackage` (it needs the test framework and `testables` wired up);
  it does travel in the `.tgz` and in git URL installs, where it can actually run.
- `Documentation~/` can never travel inside a `.unitypackage`: Unity ignores folders ending in `~`, so
  the export drops them silently. Inside the `.tgz` it is fine.
- `docs/` (the landing page) and `scripts/` (build tooling) are not part of the package.

## Uploading a release by hand

Bump `version` in `package.json`, add the matching `## [<version>]` section to `CHANGELOG.md`, build,
then:

```bash
gh release create v0.1.0 build/* --title "Multitude 0.1.0" --notes "First release"
```

Or drag both files into *Releases → Draft a new release* on GitHub. Tag names follow `v<version>`, and
the git URL install can pin them (`#v0.1.0`).

## Requirements

- macOS with a Unity Hub editor matching the `unity` field of `package.json`, activated (Unity Personal
  is enough — nothing here leaves the machine).
- `python3` (reads `package.json`, patches the manifest) and `npm` (only for the `.tgz`).


# === MVP NOTES (Documentation~/MVP.md) ===

# Multitude — MVP

Edit several prefab assets at the same time, each one in its own window, without touching the scene
you have open and without going through Unity's prefab stage.

## Install

Multitude is an editor-only package embedded in this project:

```
Packages/com.gabs.multitude/
```

Unity imports it automatically. Open the window from `Tools > Multitude > Open Selected Prefabs`, or
right click a prefab in the Project window and choose `Assets > Multitude > Open Prefab in Multitude`.

### Packaging

`./scripts/build-package.sh` runs the EditMode suite and writes `build/Multitude-<version>.unitypackage`
plus the UPM tarball. The `.unitypackage` ships `Editor/` and the manifests only: no tests, no landing
page, and `Documentation~/` can never travel inside it because Unity ignores folders ending in `~`. See
`Documentation~/BUILDING.md`.

## Usage

- **One window per prefab.** Open as many as you want; each keeps its own hierarchy, selection and
  camera. They can be docked or floated and survive a script reload (the unsaved edits do not).
- **Preview:** left drag orbits, right drag (or `Alt` + left drag) pans, the wheel zooms, `F` frames
  the prefab, `Frame` frames everything. Double click an object in the hierarchy to frame that object.
- **Editing:** select an object in the hierarchy and edit its components in the inspector, exactly as
  in the normal inspector (undo and redo work). Changes stay inside the window.
- **Apply** writes the prefab asset. **Revert** throws the changes away and reloads from disk.
- **Conflict:** if the prefab file changed on disk after you opened it, Apply refuses to overwrite and
  offers Overwrite / Keep editing / Reload from disk.
- **Closing a dirty window** asks Apply and close / Cancel / Discard and close. Cancel reopens the
  window with the session intact (Unity cannot veto a window close, so the window comes back instead).

### Particle systems and visual effects

The preview plays particle systems in edit mode: `Play` / `Pause`, `Restart`, `Loop` and a speed
slider between 0.1x and 2x. The systems are advanced by hand (`ParticleSystem.Simulate`), so nothing
depends on entering play mode. The controls only appear when the prefab has particle systems.

## How the preview stays isolated

Two rules are enforced by the implementation:

1. **Nothing of yours reaches the preview.** The window never reads the active scene, the scene view
   or the prefab stage; it only renders the session's own copy of the prefab.
2. **Nothing of Multitude reaches your scenes.** Preview copies live in the editor's hidden world with
   `HideFlags.HideAndDontSave`, on a layer reserved for them, and with `Renderer.forceRenderingOff`
   enabled, which removes them from the scene view and the game view. They are switched on only while
   the preview renders its own frame, and left over copies are destroyed when the editor reloads
   scripts.

Unity does not render preview scenes in this project's render pipeline, which is why the preview draws
a copy instead of the session content directly.

## Limits (MVP)

- Ordinary prefabs and prefab variants. Model prefabs and missing assets are rejected with a message.
- Prefabs only: scenes and ScriptableObjects are out of scope.
- Custom inspectors that assume the prefab stage or the global selection may draw incompletely; the
  window reports it instead of breaking.
- Unsaved edits do not survive a script recompile or a domain reload; the window reloads the prefab
  from disk.
- The preview updates ~0.35 s after an edit (it rebuilds the copy it renders), and while a session has
  unapplied changes the window repaints a few times per second to keep up.
- Editing a prefab asset on disk while the editor is in play mode can leave stale instances; leave play
  mode before applying external edits.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause / fix |
|---|---|
| The window says the preview is not available | The prefab no longer loads. Press `Revert` or reopen the window. |
| Nothing appears in the preview | The prefab has no renderers or colliders. A pure particle prefab needs some time to emit; press `Restart`. |
| An inspector shows a warning instead of its fields | That custom editor needs the prefab stage; edit through the fields that did draw. |
| Apply reports a conflict | The file changed on disk. Choose Overwrite only if you mean it, or Reload from disk. |


# === CHANGELOG (CHANGELOG.md) ===

# Changelog

All notable changes to this package are documented here. The format follows
[Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/) and the package uses
[Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/).

## [0.1.0] - 2026-10-26

First version, extracted from the game project it was built in.

### Added

- One editor window per prefab asset: hierarchy, isolated preview and component inspector, all
  independent between windows.
- Isolated sessions: a prefab is loaded into its own preview scene and stays clean until **Apply**;
  **Revert** reloads it from disk.
- External change protection: Apply compares the file on disk against the snapshot taken when the
  window opened and offers Overwrite, Keep editing or Reload from disk instead of overwriting silently.
- Dirty close handling with Apply and close, Cancel (the window comes back with the session intact) and
  Discard and close.
- Rotating preview: orbit, pan, zoom, frame to prefab or to a single object, selection highlight.
- Particle systems and VFX play in edit mode with Play/Pause, Restart, Loop and a speed slider.
- Resizable panes: draggable separators for the hierarchy width and the inspector height, remembered
  per window, double click to reset.
- EditMode tests for validation, session states, apply/revert/conflict, preview host and VFX playback.
